components.text: Woodland Management Plan PA3 agreement document

This is the Countryside Stewardship Woodland Management Plan (WMP) agreement document. It sets out the agreement holder specific details for a Countryside Stewardship WMP agreement. The agreement document should be read in conjunction with the following documents (which together form the Countryside Stewardship Agreement):

items.text: the Capital grants agreements: terms and conditions 2026
The supporting documents specified in this agreement document

components.text: All elements and details in this agreement document are binding on the agreement holder, unless it expressly says they are "not binding".
Objectives (not binding)

items.text: Produce a WMP in accordance with the requirements of the
PA3: Woodland management plan 2026
on GOV.UK. You must submit your plan to the Forestry Commission for approval.

components.text: Outcomes

items.text: Produce a UK Forestry Standard (UKFS) compliant WMP, plan of operations and plan maps using the Forestry Commission template and associated guidance notes from the
Applicant's guide: PA3 Woodland Management Plan 2026
on GOV.UK. A full account of historical features, important habitats, landscape and tree features must be included.

components.text: Where a felling licence is required, the plan of operations will include all proposed thinning and felling for the next 10 years, as well as the necessary detail to meet the requirements of all relevant legislation.

If the area covered by the WMP includes a Site of Special Scientific Interest (SSSI), Natural England will need to be consulted over its content while it is being drafted. Proposals must be agreed by the Forestry Commission and Natural England, and a supplementary notice of operations for the SSSI may need to be completed. If the supplementary notice is not included in the WMP, the applicant will be required to seek consent from Natural England separately.

If the WMP includes a scheduled monument or areas covered by Registered Parks or Gardens Grade II, Historic England will need to be consulted. This should be done during drafting to determine what actions may be required by Historic England to give full consent to operations included in the WMP.

Once your Countryside Stewardship agreement has been issued, the draft WMP must be submitted for approval to your local Forestry Commission admin hub. Submit your draft WMP in electronic form with supporting maps and photographs, accompanied by a completed plan submission proforma.

The maps supplied with the draft WMP should include further detail in line with the technical guidance available (see above). You are strongly advised to submit your plan to the Forestry Commission within one year from the start of your Countryside Stewardship agreement. Plans submitted later than this risk not being approved within the three-year Countryside Stewardship agreement period.

All relevant persons that have a direct interest in the land within the WMP should be allowed to see the draft plan (for example, gamekeepers or other central or local government organisations). This is so that, where appropriate, they can advise on any conflict and allow adjustments to the WMP within the three-year Countryside Stewardship agreement period.

components.text: The "Agreement Land" comprises the following land parcels.
The Countryside Stewardship terms and conditions contain separate obligations in relation to the "Agreement Land".
The following is a summary of the capital items which the agreement holder is required to deliver under the agreement:
Aim (not binding)
To produce a WMP for sustainable forest management in accordance with the UK Forestry Standard.
Eligibility

items.text: Any woodland holding over 0.5ha in area that does not currently have a management plan in place. The plan shall cover all the woodland on the holding.

The WMP must cover all the woodland on the holding, including all newly-planted woodland. The amount paid will be calculated on the entire eligible area of woodland on the holding. This calculation can include up to an additional 20% of newly-planted woodland (this means woodland that is under 10 years old at the time of application). Areas over 20% will be deducted from the total area for payment but must still be covered in the management plan.
You can find more information about eligibility in the
Applicant’s guide: PA3 Woodland management plan 2026 guidance on
on GOV.UK.

components.text: Specifications
Create the management plan using the Forestry Commission template (available on the Forestry Commission website or by request).
